tomato.soil_suitability: Well-drained, sandy loam soil with pH 6.0 to 6.8 is optimal.
tomato.fertilizer_recommendation: Apply nitrogenous fertilizer (Urea) during the vegetative stage. Transition to phosphorus-rich fertilizers (DAP) during flowering and potassium-rich ones (Potash) during fruiting.
tomato.diseases: Early Blight (Alternaria solani), Late Blight (Phytophthora infestans), Leaf Mold, Tomato Leaf Curl Virus.
tomato.irrigation_habits: Requires moderate watering. Avoid overhead sprinklers; drip irrigation is strongly recommended to prevent foliar fungal spore splash.

cotton.sowing_period: Kharif season (April-May in North India, June-July in South/Central India)
cotton.soil_suitability: Deep black clay soils (regur soils) are optimal due to high water-retention properties. Medium loam is also suitable.
cotton.fertilizer_recommendation: Requires heavy nitrogen and phosphorus. Apply split doses of Nitrogen: 50% at sowing, 25% at square formation, 25% at boll development.
cotton.diseases: Boll rot, Bacterial blight, Fusarium wilt, Leaf curl disease.
cotton.irrigation_habits: Moderate watering; crucial stages are flowering and boll development. Highly sensitive to waterlogging.

wheat.soil_suitability: Well-drained clay loam or loamy soils are ideal.
wheat.fertilizer_recommendation: Standard ratio is N:P:K at 120:60:40 kg/ha. Apply half nitrogen + full P & K at sowing; apply remaining N during first irrigation.
wheat.diseases: Yellow rust, Brown rust, Black rust, Loose smut, Powdery mildew.
wheat.irrigation_habits: Requires 4-6 irrigations. Crown Root Initiation (CRI) stage (21 days post-sowing) is the most critical stage for watering.

rice.sowing_period: Kharif season (May-June for nursery, June-July for transplanting)
rice.soil_suitability: Clayey or clay loam soils that can retain standing water are optimal.
rice.fertilizer_recommendation: 100-120 kg Nitrogen, 50-60 kg P2O5, and 40 kg K2O per hectare. Zinc sulfate (25 kg/ha) should be applied to prevent Khaira disease.
rice.diseases: Blast (Magnaporthe oryzae), Bacterial leaf blight, Sheath blight, Khaira disease (zinc deficiency).
rice.irrigation_habits: Requires standing water (2-5 cm) from transplanting until 15 days before harvest. Submergence tolerant varieties should be used in flood-prone zones.

potato.ideal_temp_c: 15-20°C for tuberization. Tuber growth stops if temp exceeds 30°C.
potato.soil_suitability: Loose, well-aerated sandy loam rich in organic matter (pH 5.2-6.4).
potato.fertilizer_recommendation: Apply well-decomposed farmyard manure (25 t/ha). NPK requirement: 120-150 kg N, 80-100 kg P, 80-100 kg K per hectare.
potato.diseases: Early Blight, Late Blight, Black scurf, Common scab.
potato.irrigation_habits: Requires frequent shallow irrigations. Maintain uniform soil moisture to prevent tuber cracking and deformities.

mustard.soil_suitability: Light to medium loam soils with good drainage; tolerates slight salinity.
mustard.fertilizer_recommendation: Apply 60-80 kg N, 30-40 kg P2O5, 20 kg K2O per hectare. Critical addition: Elemental sulfur (20-30 kg/ha) increases oil content by 15-20%.
mustard.diseases: White rust (Albugo candida), Alternaria blight, Downy mildew. Pests: Mustard aphid (Lipaphis erysimi).
mustard.irrigation_habits: Requires 2 critical irrigations: first at flowering stage (30-35 days) and second at pod formation (60-65 days). Avoid excessive moisture.

sugarcane.soil_suitability: Deep, well-drained loam or clay-loam soils with high organic matter (pH 6.5-7.5).
sugarcane.fertilizer_recommendation: Heavy feeder: 150-250 kg N, 60-80 kg P2O5, and 60-90 kg K2O per hectare applied in split doses during tillering.
sugarcane.diseases: Red rot (Colletotrichum falcatum), Smut, Grassy shoot disease.
sugarcane.irrigation_habits: High water requirement (1500-2500 mm). Alternate furrow irrigation or drip irrigation with trash mulching saves 40-50% water.

blight.environmental_triggers: Cool, damp weather with high humidity (>90%) and frequent leaf wetness.
blight.chemical_control: Spray Mancozeb (2g/L) or Copper Oxychloride (3g/L) as a protective measure. Use Metalaxyl (Ridomil MZ at 2g/L) or Azoxystrobin (1ml/L) for active infections.
blight.organic_control: Apply Trichoderma viride formulations or spray diluted neem oil (0.5%). Remove and destroy infected foliage immediately to halt spore dissemination.

rust.environmental_triggers: Cool temperatures (10-22°C) combined with morning dew, high humidity, or fog.
rust.chemical_control: Spray Propiconazole (Tilt 25 EC at 1ml/L) or Tebuconazole (Folicur at 1ml/L) immediately when pustules first appear.
rust.organic_control: Grow rust-resistant cultivars (e.g. HD-2967, DBW-187). Apply sulfur dust (25 kg/ha) or copper sulfate sprays early in the morning.

yellow_leaves.etiology: Chlorosis can arise from multiple factors: Nitrogen deficiency, Iron deficiency, overwatering/waterlogging, or viral infection.
yellow_leaves.nitrogen_deficiency: Older/lower leaves turn yellow first, starting from the tip and moving along the midrib (V-shaped yellowing). Solution: Top-dress with Urea or spray 1-2% Urea solution.
yellow_leaves.iron_deficiency: Younger/top leaves show interveinal chlorosis (veins stay green while leaf turns yellow/white). Common in alkaline or calcareous soils. Solution: Foliar spray of Ferrous Sulfate (0.5%) with citric acid.
yellow_leaves.overwatering_root_rot: General limp yellowing across entire plant accompanied by stunted growth. Solution: Improve drainage, reduce irrigation intervals, and drench roots with Trichoderma or Carbendazim (1g/L).

pest_control.sucking_pests: Aphids, Whiteflies, Thrips, Jassids. Spray Neem oil (10,000 ppm at 2-3 ml/L) or Imidacloprid 17.8 SL (0.5 ml/L) or Acetamiprid 20 SP (0.2 g/L).
pest_control.chewing_borers: Stem borers, Fruit borers, Fall armyworm. Install yellow sticky traps and pheromone traps (5/acre). Spray Bacillus thuringiensis (Bt @ 2g/L) or Chlorantraniliprole 18.5 SC (Coragen @ 0.4 ml/L).
pest_control.ipm_practices: Practice crop rotation, maintain field sanitation, encourage natural predators (ladybird beetles, chrysoperla), and avoid prophylactic broad-spectrum insecticide sprays.

drip_irrigation.water_efficiency: Saves 40% to 60% water compared to conventional flood irrigation; increases crop yield by 20% to 35%.
drip_irrigation.fertigation_advantage: Allows direct liquid nutrient delivery to the crop root zone (fertigation), reducing fertilizer losses through leaching and volatilization by 30-40%.
drip_irrigation.disease_reduction: Keeps plant canopy and foliage completely dry, drastically lowering foliar fungal spore germination (e.g. Blight, Downy Mildew, Rust).

organic_farming.jeevamrit_formulation: Mix 10 kg fresh cow dung, 10 L cow urine, 2 kg jaggery, 2 kg gram flour (besan), and a handful of fertile soil in 200 L water. Ferment for 48 hours. Apply 200 L/acre via irrigation.
organic_farming.soil_enrichment: Apply well-decomposed vermicompost (5-8 t/ha) or farmyard manure (FYM). Sow green manure crops like Sunnhemp or Dhaincha and incorporate into soil before flowering.
organic_farming.pest_repellents: Prepare Dashparni ark or Neem-garlic extract for broad-spectrum organic insect deterrence.

frost_protection.immediate_measures: Give a light irrigation to the field in the evening before an expected frosty night. Wet soil conducts and retains heat significantly better than dry soil, raising canopy micro-temperature by 1.5-2.5°C.
frost_protection.smudge_smoke: Burn crop residue or damp straw along field borders on the upwind side to form an insulating smoke blanket that prevents radiant heat loss.
frost_protection.foliar_protection: Spray dilute soluble sulfur (0.1%) or Glucose/Potassium nitrate solution (0.2%) to bolster cell sap concentration against ice crystal nucleation.

soil_testing.sampling_protocol: Collect V-shaped sub-samples (0-15 cm depth for field crops, 0-30 cm for horticulture) from 8-10 random spots per hectare in a zig-zag pattern. Mix thoroughly, air dry in shade, and prepare 500g composite sample.
soil_testing.key_parameters: pH (acidity/alkalinity), Electrical Conductivity (salinity), Organic Carbon (fertility indicator), Available N, P, K, and micronutrients (Zinc, Iron, Boron, Sulfur).

sar_radar.concept: Sentinel-1 Synthetic Aperture Radar (SAR) is an active spaceborne microwave sensor operating at C-band (5.405 GHz, ~5.5 cm wavelength).
sar_radar.all_weather_capability: Microwaves penetrate clouds, dense fog, haze, smoke, and operate 24/7 day and night, providing reliable continuous Earth observation when optical satellites (Sentinel-2) are blinded by monsoon overcast.
sar_radar.soil_moisture_vv: Co-polarization backscatter (VV in dB) is highly sensitive to the surface dielectric constant, directly tracking soil moisture saturation, flood inundation, and root-zone water deficits.
sar_radar.canopy_biomass_vh: Cross-polarization backscatter (VH in dB) measures volume scattering from crop stems and leaves, tracking crop biomass accumulation, vegetative canopy expansion, and lodging damage.
sar_radar.radar_vegetation_index: Radar Vegetation Index (RVI = 4*VH/(VV+VH)) tracks plant structural density from bare soil (0.0) to peak vegetative maturity (~1.0).
sar_radar.field_application: Use SAR to automate cloud-proof irrigation schedules, detect post-storm crop lodging, delineate flooded acreage, and calculate satellite-verified field water stress without manual sensors.

fertilizer.urea: 46% Nitrogen. Promotes rapid vegetative growth. High leaf chlorophyll density.
fertilizer.dap: 18% Nitrogen, 46% Phosphorus. Supports early root establishment and robust flowering.
fertilizer.potash: 60% Potassium (MOP). Enhances plant immune systems, crop weight, sugar accumulation, and drought tolerance.
fertilizer.npk_general: Apply balanced ratios according to regional crop recommendations. Excess nitrogen causes watery stems and invites pest attacks.

soil_ph.acidic_fix: Apply agricultural lime (calcium carbonate) or dolomite lime. Dolomite is preferred if soil test indicates magnesium deficiency.
soil_ph.alkaline_fix: Incorporate elemental sulfur or gypsum. Organic mulch and compost buffer alkaline soils by generating weak acids during decomposition.
soil_ph.nutrient_availability: Optimal nutrient assimilation occurs between pH 6.0 and 7.0. Iron and zinc become locked in highly alkaline soils.
